newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent seen weaker, downside targets ey.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent seen weaker, downside targets ey.

text.p: ARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* Sentiment continues bearish with chartists eyeing downside targets although the market's oversold condition could still provide a short term bounce.
* "It's possible that we will see $17 this week but the longer term target could be as low as $15.50".
IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures sentiment continues bearish with chartists eyeing downside targets although the market's oversold condition could still provide a short term bounce, analysts said.

Steve Kwan of MMS International Standard and Poors said Tuesdays "bearish outside day" pattern on the charts where the high-low range was wider than the previous day's was reflective of the negative sentiment in the market since last Friday's break of $18.

"It's possible that we will see $17 this week but the longer term target could be as low as $15.50," Kwan said, the longer term objective coming from a swing back from the double-top at around $20.60 and through the mid-point at around $18.00.
Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson Isle of Man set a very short term target at around $17.30 which represents an extension of the market's previous downtrend line from the beginning of the year.
He said from there 2-3 week objectives were $16.05 and $15.08 on a swing retracement based off the break point at $17.85.
"The market's a bit overdone to the downside but any technical bounce will be capped at the $17.85 area, yesterday's high and breakpoint to the downside," Wilson said.
Wilson saw short term targets to the downside for July gas oil at $160 then $156 and $151 with any bounce capped at $167.50 the top of a gap on the July chart from three days ago.
IPE June gas oil closed $1.50 firmer at $161.50 a tonne on Tuesday with the July contract at $162.75.

IPE Brent crude dipped in late trade to a 12-month low as an early bounce evaporated amid talk of rising U.S. product stocks. July Brent closed down 6 cents at $17.50 a barrel, the lowest seen on the prompt contract since May 1996, extending a $2-slide since the beginning of June.
Rising U.S. crude and gasoline stocks gave investment funds an excuse to bale out of the market last Friday and this week's API figures could again set short-term market direction.
Tuesday's API report showed refinery runs had stayed high, fuelling a bearish rise in gasoline stocks.

The 2.7 million barrel rise in unleaded inventories that brought stocks to 202.4 million was enough to drag July unleaded down about 0.20 cent in ACCESS trade from a settlement of 56.40 cents a gallon.

Traders expected the stock rise to add further pressure today but pointed out that much of the bearishness was already built in with crude and products prices having fallen around 15 percent in the last two weeks.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
